Ensemble Labs / Research statement

Better ways for people and agents to work together.

We explore how shared context, multiplayer collaboration, and new ways of building software can help humans and AI become better teammates.

Read the vision ↓

Why Ensemble

An ensemble is a group of separate people, systems, or parts that work together to form a complete and harmonious unit.

Today, most AI work is single-player: one person and one agent in a private thread. The result may be useful, but the context, decisions, and working method rarely become part of the team’s shared intelligence.

We believe the more consequential opportunity is collective. People and agents should be able to understand the same environment, participate in the same work, and improve how they collaborate over time.

ENSEMBLE /ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl/

“Together” in French. Distinct parts, made more capable in relation.

One product

Atlas

A shared place for company knowledge and the agents that put it to work.

Atlas brings context and collaboration into one system. Its two parts can stand alone, but become more useful when they learn from the same company environment.

Atlas Knowledge

A shared context layer for the company’s knowledge, skills, decisions, and permissions—made useful to people and agents alike.

Atlas Agents

Multiplayer agents that work with the team in Slack, participating in the same conversations and drawing from the same company context.

A model for collaboration

Less AI manner. More useful teammate.

Generic models are trained to answer. Working well with people asks for something more specific.

We are developing our own fine-tuned models based on Kimi for human collaboration: concise, candid, context-aware, and free of the filler and mannered prose people learn to tune out.

Base
Kimi
Approach

Focus

What better collaboration requires

The goal is not autonomous spectacle. It is more legible, capable, and meaningful work between people and machines.

Shared, not private.
Important context and decisions should remain visible to the people doing the work.
Context before autonomy.
Useful agency starts with a grounded understanding of the company, its methods, and its constraints.
Human judgment stays present.
Collaboration should increase what people can understand, decide, and create—not move them outside the system.
Work where work happens.
The best interface is often the conversation, codebase, or tool a team already shares.

Our aim

Help companies become better ensembles.

Not organizations where agents replace people, or people supervise a fleet from the outside. Organizations where each contributes what it does best, from the same context, toward shared outcomes.

Better context. Better coordination. Better ways to build together.
